![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14216490/assets/559a6b6cb717c10e60b77da402e310fc5895c814655b4ca1748eba294d712a32.png)

Evaluate ${\int }_{C}\frac{1}{2}xy\,\text{d}y,$ where $C$ is the path along the upper half of the circle of radius $2,$ traversed from the point $(2,0)$ to the point $(-2,0),$ as shown above.
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y={\int }_{a}^{b}f(r(t))\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t.
$$

The curve $C$ is a half of a circle of radius $2$ centered at $O.$ It can be parameterized as 

$$
r(t)=⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,0\le t\le \pi .
$$

Computing $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t},$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=\frac{1}{2}xy,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =\frac{1}{2}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(r(t))\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot (2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\cdot \text{d}t \\  & =4{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this using the substitution $u=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,$ $\text{d}u=-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t\,\text{d}t & =4{\int }_{1}^{-1}{u}^{2}\,(-\text{d}u) \\  & =4{\int }_{-1}^{1}{u}^{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{4}{3}{u}^{3}{|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}[(1)^{3}-(-1)^{3}] \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
